items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: Mr. Dent, everytime that dinnertime come, he'd say, 'Come on, boys, and sit at the table. Come on out here and eat.' And he would feed us.

ctx.x: We ventured out one year through northern Alabama, up to Chattanooga, Tennessee, and we got stranded in Chattanooga, Tennessee. We were stopping at a hotel called the Dent Hotel. And this is one of the reasons why I love people today, because people have been good to me all my life. When I say me, I mean good to us musicians all of our lives.

We stayed in that hotel. We didn't have money to pay for food -- to pay for food. And Mr. Dent, everytime that dinnertime come, he'd say, 'Come on, boys, and sit at the table. Come on out here and eat.' And he would feed us. And I can remember how we got out of that town. We had two saxophones in the band then. We had a boy named Philander Tiller from Little Rock who I had recommended to join the band. Fernando Tiller had been going to Howard University, and this particular year he had laid out of school.
